description: ECB-supervised significant institutions in Slovenia are outside the national fit-and-proper publication channel, and no substitute person-level source was established.
Payment institutions and e-money institutions: their management-body approvals by Banka Slovenije were not confirmed to be published in the same way as bank board authorisations.
No historical archive of removed vacancy postings was identified for any of the three supervisors; expired posts appear to be deleted rather than archived.

Adjacent Slovenian bodies that also generate financial-sector leadership and organisational events were not covered in this cell: SDH (state asset manager, appoints supervisory boards of state-owned banks/insurers), the Bank Assets Management Company successor arrangements, the deposit-guarantee and resolution functions, and the Ministry of Finance's directorate for the financial system.
Internal reorganisation of the supervisors is only weakly observable — inferred from unit names in vacancy adverts and from org-chart pages, with no announced change log.
English-language coverage of these sources is partial: BS and GOV.SI maintain /en/ mirrors, but ATVP, AZN and Uradni list appointment decisions are effectively Slovenian-only.

No first-party source identified yet for BKS Bank AG bančna podružnica, UniCredit Banka Slovenija, Deželna banka Slovenije (DBS) and N Banka — all appear in Slovenian bank listings but were not covered by the cell's seed actor list.
Jobs/hiring topic is under-covered: bank career portals and vacancy feeds ('kariera', 'prosta delovna mesta', 'zaposlitev') were not enumerated.

Statutory registers that record board membership changes (AJPES / sodni register, and Bank of Slovenia fit-and-proper decisions) were referenced only indirectly; no concrete register endpoints were captured for the cell.

English-language corporate feeds (NLB Group EN newsroom, Addiko Group AG ad-hoc disclosures, OTP Group Budapest investor releases) were not separately captured, although they often carry the same board news for the Slovenian subsidiaries.

Cash-handling and cash-in-transit / cash-cycle suppliers to SI banks (e.g. cash automation, CIT operators, safe/recycler vendors) were not reached in this run; only ATM/self-service OEMs and software integrators were covered.

Bank-side procurement/tender evidence for private banks was not pursued (out of cell), but supplier-side signals would be much easier to interpret if paired with e-JN / bank RFP notices where the bank is state-linked (SID banka, SDH-owned entities).
Several candidate URLs are inferred rather than fetched (payten.si, printecgroup.com careers path, mojedelo.com), and no URL in this slice was liveness-verified.

Regional-language coverage (hr/sr/bs) was only incidental, yet ASEE/Payten, Comtrade and ASEE Solutions publish group careers and appointment news in Croatian and Serbian, often before any SI-language version.
No systematic channel was identified for detecting delivery-centre openings or office expansions by foreign vendors in Slovenia (lease/real-estate, municipal or investment-agency announcements).

Hungarian- and Italian-language HQ channels were not searched in this pass. OTP's Budapest disclosures and Intesa's Italian releases can carry SI subsidiary appointments hours to days before the English version, and some organisational items never get an English translation.

Non-bank foreign-parent entities in SI were only lightly covered: Sparkasse Leasing, S-Factoring, Erste Card Slovenija, Addiko's SI leasing arm, and card/acquiring processors. These have leadership changes with real market relevance but no press rooms.

The primary Slovenian company register (AJPES / ePRS / sodni register) was not directly located in this pass - only commercial aggregators mirroring it. The primary register is the legally authoritative record of board and representative changes.

Bank of Slovenia fit-and-proper approval decisions are referenced in subsidiary press releases ('subject to approval of the Bank of Slovenia') but no dedicated decisions register or ECB SSM decisions feed for SI significant institutions was profiled here.

The 'jobs / hiring' topic is weakly served by this cell. Foreign parents rarely publish SI vacancy or headcount information; only LinkedIn (collection-restricted) and subsidiary career pages would carry it, and subsidiary career portals were not enumerated.

No web-archive strategy was profiled. Group press rooms prune older items and subsidiary sites are rebranded after mergers (SKB and Nova KBM pages folded into otpbanka.si), which silently destroys historical appointment evidence.

Smaller SI banks and savings banks (Delavska hranilnica, Addiko Bank Slovenija, Banka Sparkasse, Dezelna banka Slovenije, Hranilnica LON, Primorska hranilnica Vipava, N banka legacy entity, BKS Bank branch) have no mapped statutory-disclosure landing page.

The payments half of sector=both is represented only by Bankart. Other SI payments/fintech filers - licensed payment institutions, e-money issuers, account information service providers listed in the BSI register, plus card/POS vendors and processing ISVs - have no filings mapped.

Standalone remuneration reports ('porocilo o prejemkih') under the SI implementation of SRD II were not separately located for any bank; only Pillar 3 remuneration templates and in-annual-report sections were found.
English-language coverage of this cell rests almost entirely on NLB, which publishes parallel EN filings; most other SI banks' statutory documents appear to exist in Slovenian only.
AJPES JOLP is the backbone of this cell but imposes a documented ~20-entity-per-day per-username view limit and requires registration, which constrains any bulk annual sweep.

No conference/awards source was found that specifically covers the card-processing and payment-infrastructure actors (Bankart, Halcom, Margento, Petrol/Mercator loyalty-payments units). Bankart appears only as a co-presenter in ZBS press activity, not as an event host with its own speaker roster.

Most conference sites in this cell overwrite the previous year's speaker page (exception: DSI, which uses per-year subdomains). Without archiving, the year-on-year title-diffing that makes this cell valuable is impossible.

University-pipeline coverage is concentrated on University of Ljubljana faculties (EF, FRI, FE, FMF). University of Maribor (EPF, FERI) and University of Primorska (FAMNIT) career centres and their bank scholarship calls were not systematically checked, despite NKBM/OTP's Maribor base.
Conference programmes are frequently distributed as PDFs and speaker bios as images/slide decks, which a plain HTML scraper will miss entirely.

The regional events most likely to feature Slovenian payments leadership (Money Motion, Balkan Business Analysis Conference) publish primarily in English/Croatian, so Slovenian-language monitoring alone will miss them, while Slovenian trade press covers them only sporadically.

Company-level bank unions beyond NLB — at OTP banka (post-merger, covering former Nova KBM and SKB units), Addiko, Delavska hranilnica, Sberbank/N Banka successor entities, Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit and Gorenjska banka — were not individually located, although SBS lists several as member unions.

Two workforce-side institutions were identified conceptually but not yet located as concrete sources: the Ekonomsko-socialni svet (tripartite social and economic council, where sector disputes escalate) and the Inšpektorat RS za delo (IRSD), whose annual reports aggregate labour-law violations by activity.

ZRSZ and SURS both publish at SKD sector level (K = financial and insurance activities), which merges banking with insurance and other finance. No banking-only (K64) monthly employment series was located, and the SKD 2008 to SKD 2025 changeover on 1 January 2025 breaks comparability.

The topic 'leadership moves' is only weakly served by this cell. Union and labour-market sources cover rank-and-file headcount, not management appointments; management-board changes are disclosed through supervisory-board and regulatory channels outside this cell.
The cell rationale flags outsourcing as a harm channel, but no Slovenian source specific to bank IT/back-office outsourcing or shared-service-centre transfers of staff was found.

Most candidates were identified through search-result metadata; only the SBS homepage was fetched directly. Liveness, feed availability and robots/ToS constraints are therefore unconfirmed for the remainder.
The three highest-value channels in this cell (SeeNews, Central Banking, Bloomberg) are wholly or partly paywalled, and STA's full wire is subscription-only.
FinTech Futures (403) and Total Slovenia News (525) could not be retrieved with a plain fetcher.

Vendor/PSP-side Slovenian appointments (Bankart, Paywiser, Mbills, processing and core-banking suppliers) are thinly covered by English trade press; the only signals found were LinkedIn posts and one-off trade items.
Cross-border aggregators cover appointments well but carry almost nothing on Slovenian banking JOB POSTINGS, headcount or hiring volumes; only generic English-speaking-jobs portals surfaced.
The cell's rationale relies on aggregators archiving items after local pages expire; this was assumed, not tested.

No career page was located this pass for several remaining SI deposit-takers and bank-adjacent entities: Hranilnica Vipava's peers, N Banka (merged, status of legacy pages unchecked), Sberbank/N banka successor entities, SID banka (development bank), SKB Leasing, Summit Leasing / Nova KBM leasing arms, and the Slovenian branches of foreign banks operating cross-border.

Two of the largest employers' vacancy feeds remain unread: OTP banka (FledgeHR, redirect loop) and UniCredit Banka Slovenija (JS-rendered shell). NLB's Cornerstone job-list route was inferred but not observed.
No lexicon yet exists to classify Slovenian job titles into the cell's target functions (IT, payments, cards, digital channels, compliance, ATM/branch network).
MojeDelo.com was confirmed as the de-facto vacancy channel for at least BKS Bank and Primorska hranilnica Vipava, but no concrete MojeDelo employer-profile URLs were captured for any bank.

This cell's sources surface open ROLES well but capture executive/leadership appointments only incidentally (e.g. DBS 'regijski direktor' vacancy). Board-level and management-board changes are not published as vacancies.
Career pages show only current vacancies; removed postings are unrecoverable and no source in this cell provides history.
Commercial aggregators (Optius, MojeDelo, Careerjet, BetterCareer) are the only route to the long tail, but their ToS/robots were not reviewed and are likely to restrict automated collection.

The full licensed population of Slovenian payment institutions and e-money institutions has not been enumerated — only sample entities (Paywiser, mBills) were confirmed from the Banka Slovenije registers.
Acquirers, POS/terminal estate operators and ATM operators in Slovenia (beyond Bankart) were not searched — e.g. independent ATM deployers, merchant-acquiring arms, terminal service providers.
Slovenian business and tech media were not directly reached: Finance.si, STA, Računalniške novice, Delo, Bankirai/Bančni vestnik were not confirmed as accessible sources for appointment news.
Only Workable was identified as an ATS in use. Which ATS each cell actor runs (Greenhouse, Lever, SmartRecruiters, Recruitee, Teamtailor, SAP SuccessFactors for Nexi) is unmapped.

Local terms were used for careers, register and appointment concepts, but not for acquiring/scheme-migration role vocabulary (e.g. 'ISO 20022 migracija', 'kartično poslovanje', 'procesni center', 'vodja razvoja plačil').
MojeDelo.com, Zaposlitev.info, Deloglasnik, Kariera, Competo and Rekruter were named by ZRSZ but their per-company URL patterns for the cell's actors were not established.

All confirmed register sources expose current state (who is a representative now, which entities are licensed now). No confirmed source provides a historical time series of representative changes with effective dates, other than the eObjave publication stream, which has a limited retention window.

AZN (Agencija za zavarovalni nadzor, insurance supervision) registers were not searched. Bancassurance and insurance-adjacent payments employers therefore fall outside the enumerated population if the sector definition includes them.

Banka Slovenije must approve bank management board members (dovoljenje za opravljanje funkcije clana uprave banke). No published list or decision feed of such approvals was located, although it would be the single most precise leadership-move source in the SI banking sector.
Register sources use different identifiers (maticna stevilka in AJPES, entity names in BS registers, LEI in EBA registers). No confirmed crosswalk was established.

Only the JOLP daily cap (20 entities/user/day) was concretely documented. Robots.txt and terms-of-use for ajpes.si, bsi.si, a-tvp.si and euclid.eba.europa.eu were not reviewed, so automated collection is not yet cleared.
MojeDelo.com structure (category URLs, RSS, filters, robots.txt, ad volume for banking and IT) is entirely undocumented because the fetch failed.
The statutory national vacancy register (PoiščiDelo.si) is login-gated, so the near-census of SI employers - including micro vendors in cards, POS and ATM servicing - is not openly collectable.

Several named SI portals and agency vacancy pages were identified but not fetched in this pass: BetterCareer.si, Slo-Tech /delo, Računalniške novice job section, Adecco.si, si.trenkwalder.com, Manpower/Competo/Dekra/ProHuman SI sites.

LinkedIn - in practice a dominant channel for SI banking and fintech vacancies and the main visible surface for leadership moves - was not covered in this cell's scope and no compliant collection route was assessed.

The same vacancy is likely syndicated across ESS, Optius, MojeDelo, Zaposlitev.info and agency sites, and no dedup key or occupation-code mapping (SKD activity codes, PDM-1 occupation fields) has been defined.

English-language vacancy surfaces for Slovenia were only lightly explored (EURES and ESS English mirrors); English-first tech job boards used by SI fintechs for international hiring were not identified.

No archival or time-series route for SI vacancy ads was established; all identified sources expose only currently-open positions, so hiring trend analysis over time is impossible without self-built history.

LinkedIn company pages were confirmed for NLB Group, Banka Slovenije, Intesa Sanpaolo SI, Bankart and Halcom, but not for OTP banka Slovenija, SKB (OTP), Addiko Bank, Delavska hranilnica, Gorenjska banka, Sberbank successor entities, or SI PSPs/fintechs (Mercury/Sedmi val, Payten SI, Nexi SI entity).
No ATS-level feeds identified (Workday/SmartRecruiters/Successfactors tenants used by SI banks), which would give structured, dated, machine-readable vacancy data instead of scraped boards.

Slovenian-language searching worked for job boards and media, but no local-language equivalent was found for 'placement announcement' as a genre; the glossary term set for recruiter announcements in Slovenian remains thin.
This cell can surface claimed moves but not confirm them; statutory confirmation of bank board changes lives in AJPES/court register and Banka Slovenije notices, which are outside this cell.
The two highest-value channels in this cell (LinkedIn, Glassdoor) both prohibit scraping and gate content, so no compliant automated collection route has been established.
No paywalled-archive access strategy defined for Finance, Delo, Dnevnik and Večer — the four outlets most likely to carry the substantive detail behind an appointment.

Payments-sector (non-bank) personnel coverage is thin: searches surfaced banks and state holdings, but almost nothing on payment institutions, card processors, or fintech leadership in Slovenian media.

Only one regional daily (Večer) is represented; regional and local outlets covering savings banks and cooperative banks (Delavska hranilnica, Deželna banka Slovenije network, Primorska/Gorenjska titles) were not enumerated.

Social/professional channels where Slovenian bank appointments are announced first — LinkedIn posts by banks and executives, and outlets' own X/Facebook feeds (e.g. Bloomberg Adria Slovenija) — were observed in search results but not developed into structured sources.
No archive/back-file source identified for building a multi-year appointments time series (needed to compute tenure and turnover rates).
Slovenian-language versions of several association governance pages (notably ZBS) were not resolved to working URLs in this pass; findings lean on the English mirrors, which may lag.

Association committees below board level (ZBS working committees for payments, AML, ESG, digital euro) were not enumerated — they are the layer where operational bank leaders sit and where sector-agenda shifts appear earliest.
No archival/historical view of association board composition was established, so a diff-based collector starting now cannot date changes that occurred before it was deployed.
The highest-velocity appointment and secretariat-hiring channel (LinkedIn association pages) cannot be collected automatically under its ToS.
Bilateral chambers other than AmCham and AHK (British-Slovenian, French, Italian, Nordic) and the employers' association ZDS (Združenje delodajalcev Slovenije) were not searched in this pass.

CPV-code map for banking/payments/IT-staffing procurement in Slovenia has not been fixed. Without an agreed CPV list (e.g. 66110000 banking services, 66172000 payment transaction processing, 72xxxxxx IT services, 30162000 smart cards, 79600000 recruitment services), portal and TED queries will be ad hoc and non-reproducible.

The actor list of Slovenian state / state-influenced financial entities is only partially enumerated here (UJP, FURS, MF, Banka Slovenije, SID banka, SDH, KAD, Modra zavarovalnica). Missing candidates include NLB and other SDH-held banks and insurers, AJPES, KDD, ZPIZ, and the Ministry of Finance's directorates.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin by nature: javni natečaj notices and razpisna dokumentacija are Slovene-only; only TED provides English summaries, and those omit the staffing detail.

The March 2026 shift of gazette announcements away from Uradni list means the pre-2026 archive and the post-2026 stream live in different places, risking a discontinuity in any time series of state hiring/tendering.

No URL in this slice has been fetched and confirmed live; several (bsi.si/razpisi/kadrovski-razpisi, the gov.si Delovna mesta aggregator, kapitalska-druzba.si over http) are reconstructed from search-result descriptions rather than observed page structure.
Robots.txt / terms-of-use posture has not been checked for enarocanje.si, ejn.gov.si, dkom.si, ess.gov.si and the commercial aggregators.
